next_event.source: No investor day or framework update found in Baba FY2027-label transcripts; CEO on 2026-09-14: 'We are not going to guide 2027' (Goldman Sachs Global Consumer and Retail Conference, document_id 221001). Next event is the Q3 fiscal 2026 call (date not in corpus); fiscal 2027 guidance would come with Q4 in about March or April 2027.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Target is a 15% non-GAAP EBIT (operating) margin from the PVH+ Plan (2022; an analyst described it on 2023-09-12, document_id 88376, as '15% EBIT target by 2025'). The 2025 date lapsed (CFO, 2024-04-02: 'may take a year or two longer'); last management restatement found was 'medium term' (2025-09-04). Fiscal 2026 guide is about 8.8% operating margin, 11% excluding gross tariffs. Comparisons below use consensus operating margin, not EBITDA. PVH fiscal year ends about Feb 1; Baba labels by end year (Baba FY2027 = PVH fiscal 2026).

statements.quote: I think, though, with respect to timing of achieving the 15%, our expectations for 2024 obviously makes our 2025 target timing exceedingly difficult. The PVH+ Plan and the five growth drivers are absolutely the right strategy for us to drive sustainable, long-term profitable growth. And importantly, given our progress across the P&L, our path to the 15% remains fully intact, even if it may take a year or two longer.

street.gap_assumption: No target year, so the gap uses the last full consensus year with an operating margin row: Baba FY2029 (PVH fiscal 2028) operating margin 8.48% vs 15%, so +652 bps (data_compute). Consensus operating margin: 8.83% FY2026 (actual), 8.75% FY2027 (equals the ~8.8% guide), 8.44% FY2028, 8.48% FY2029; FY2030 8.78% from operating income over revenue. EBITDA margins shown by FY are consensus EBITDA/revenue. The street models no expansion at all.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 fiscal 2026, Q2 fiscal 2026], operating margin. Q1 6.5% vs 8.1% (document_id 45048; VA 1QFY-2026). Q2 reported 11.1% includes about 510 bps of tariff refunds (interim CFO Stone, document_id 217510); excluding refunds about 6.0% vs 8.2%. Q3 guided about 7.5%. Spring 2027 Europe order book down mid-single digits. About $45M of annualized cost savings confirmed. LTM EBITDA margin 12.1% is approximate (Q2 revenue derived from the reported -3% and Q2 D&A from the VA estimate) and includes the refunds.

verdict: Rubric 8, but a weak GXO match: the only catalyst is a new external CFO under a five-year CEO, and the 15% EBIT target already missed its 2025 date and is no longer reaffirmed.
open_questions: Will new CFO Alexis Rollier reset or drop the 15% EBIT target when fiscal 2027 guidance is given (about March 2027)?
How much of the 2.2-point gap between guided 11% ex-tariff and 8.8% reported margin is recoverable versus permanent tariff cost?
With Europe wholesale orders down mid-single digits, can margin expand at all without revenue growth?
